paragraphs.text: Official DeepSeek Chat inside DSH Desktop: one sidebar panel, the real chat.deepseek.com page, and a
session that survives restarts. No Electron internals, no chat reimplementation.
# dsh-desktop-chat
Opens the official **DeepSeek Chat** web app (`chat.deepseek.com`) inside **DeepSeek Harness Desktop

**, in the
center panel, through the desktop's native browser guest. One sidebar entry, the real pag

e, and the session
survives closing the app.
**Español** → README.es.md
*The entry registers as one more DSH panel. Icon, label and selected state belong to the shell; the

plugin
only provides the destination.*
*The official page inside the center panel: not a clone, not an iframe. The native guest keeps the s

ession
and the page state while you switch panels.*
## What it does

- Adds a **Chat DeepSeek** entry to the DSH Desktop sidebar.
- Renders `https://chat.deepseek.com/`

in the center panel, with the official interface untouched.
- Restores the session on startup, so yo

u do not sign in every time you open DSH.
- Keeps the page alive when you switch panels: hiding and

reopening neither reloads it nor drops the login.
- Ships diagnostics (`GET /api/dsh-desktop-chat/st
ate`) and a route to forget the saved session.
## What it does not do

- It does not reimplement the chat or replace the official site with its own interface.
- It does no

t turn DeepSeek into a model provider, an agent or an automation tool.
- It does not touch your exis

ting DSH models, agents, plugins or providers.
- It does not store passwords, read your personal bro

wser profile, or send credentials anywhere.
- It cannot keep `HttpOnly` cookies: DSH does not expose
a guest partition's cookie store to plugins.
## Requirements
- **DSH Desktop** `>= 0.2.1-rc.3`, profile `desktop` (a plain web profile provides no native browser

guest).
- Windows 11 (tested); macOS and Linux untested.
- No runtime dependencies; no separate Nod
e installation required.

Restart DSH Desktop after installing. The entry appears in the sidebar as **Chat DeepSeek**.
## Usage

1. Click **Chat DeepSeek** in the sidebar: the page loads in the center panel.
2. Sign in once, manu

ally, on the official site.
3. Come back whenever you want (hiding and reopening the panel neither r

eloads the page nor signs you out).
4. After restarting DSH, the plugin restores the page state befo
re showing it: you should still be signed in.
If the sign-in screen appears after a restart, check the diagnostics below before signing in again:

it will
tell you whether the snapshot is being written, and why not.
## What is kept and what is not
DSH Desktop gives every browser view a **process-lifetime session partition** (a new random name on

each
start). A plugin cannot change that, and there is no public API to read the partition's cookies

. The session
is therefore preserved at the page level:
| Data | Kept? | Where |
| `chat.deepseek.com` `localStorage` (includes `userToken`) | Yes | `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\dsh-desktop-

chat\session.json` (or `$DSH_HOME`) |
| Cookies the page can see (`document.cookie`) | Yes | same fi

le |
| `HttpOnly` cookies (WAF/Cloudflare: `cf_clearance`, `aws-waf-token`…) | **No** | unreachable

from a plugin in this DSH |
| Passwords | Never | — |
Honest consequence: DeepSeek authenticates with the token in `localStorage`, so the session should s

urvive.
Losing the WAF cookies may trigger an anti-bot check after a restart; that is up to the site
e WAF cookies may trigger an anti-bot check after a restart; that is up to the site, not the plugin.

## How it works
- **Host half** (`lib/index.js`, DSH Host process): registers four routes on `ctx.webServer`, writes

the
snapshot atomically with user-only permissions, and never imports `electron`. Details and evide

nce in
docs/architecture.md.
- **Browser half** (`lib/client.js`): registers the sidebar row (`sideb

ar.panellist`) and the panel (`main`)
under one id, reserves a native guest, and keeps the `<webview

>` outside the React tree so hiding the panel
does not destroy it.
- **Restore**: on the page's orig

in it writes `localStorage` and `document.cookie`, reloads once, and from
then on saves every 10 s a

nd whenever the panel is hidden.
- **Guards**: a save with no session cannot overwrite a snapshot th

at had one; an explicit sign-out does
clear it.
## Compatibility

| DSH | `>= 0.2.1-rc.3` (the only version tested by the author) |
| Node | `>= 22` |
| OS | Windows

11 (tested); macOS and Linux untested |
| Profile | `desktop` (the web profile has no native guest)

|
| Catalog | listed on dsh-plugin.org |
| `@jaychang1989/dsh-webchat` | not required; do not run bo

| listed on dsh-plugin.org |
| `@jaychang1989/dsh-webchat` | not required; do not run both at once |
Validation status: **tested on Windows 11 with DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.3** (2026-10-25). Manual sign-in

in the
panel, full DSH exit, restart, and the session was still active: on the new start the plugin

restored 27
keys — token included — before loading the page, which opened without asking for creden

tials. Hiding and
reshowing the panel keeps the same page (the guest is not remounted).
Not validated: macOS, Linux, other DSH versions, and the behaviour if DeepSeek starts requiring `Htt

macOS, Linux, other DSH versions, and the behaviour if DeepSeek starts requiring `HttpOnly`
cookies.
